EDIT, I finally understand the reason behind why the script above fails to work. It is because Date is a continuous set of variables (numeric) while the other 2 are discrete (strings), right? Either way, I would still like a way to express the information in the way I originally intended. I would like to be bars next to the corresponding tip, each corresponding to a column, with the Date column being a continuous scale, that way it is easier to interpret. Is there a way to modify my code above? Or is there a superior method of achieving what I want?

On Friday, April 9, 2021 at 1:17:26 PM UTC+10 Yasir Kusay wrote:
Hello,

Is there a way of mapping linked metadata to appear next to the accession number. I can currently do this using geom_label to include all the information I want to include, but I want this to be colour coded instead, using bars. Using geom_tiplab(aes(color=COLNAME), geom="label", .....) for this brings partial success (though I want to remove the accession number from it). However, trying to include a total of 3 columns (Region, Strain and Date, the last column I want to have a continuous colour scale for) fails to work, and the error returned is as follows:

"Error: Continuous value supplied to discrete scale".

The code that results in this is:
p %<+% dataframe + geom_tiplab(aes(color=Region), size=1) + geom_tiplab(aes(fill = Strain), size = 1, offset=.01, geom="label", label.padding = unit(0, "lines"), label.size = 0) + geom_tiplab(aes(color=Date), size=1) # + scale_fill_continuous(low='darkblue', high='red')
(Please notice the #, which comments out the scale information).
I noticed that including the geom_tiplab for Date always brings about that error (except when used alone). Could I get assistance as to why that is?
